exercise.title: Why do some elementary series live on the whole line and others do not?

statement.p: The series for e^x, \sin x, and \cos x are valid for every real x, while \ln(1+x) and \arctan x are not. In your own words, why is that not a defect of the functions, and what is the series actually reporting?

hint.p: Factorials in the denominator overpower any fixed power of x. Geometric-type series are limited by a radius coming from a nearby singularity or from the original geometric seed, even if the function itself is defined more widely.

exercise.title: Why is the binomial series a Taylor series?

statement.p: The binomial series for (1+x)^p comes from matching derivatives at 0, and it recovers the geometric series when p=-1. In your own words, why does that make the geometric series part of the Taylor library rather than a rival construction, and why must |x|<1 still be respected?

hint.p: The coefficients are exactly the Taylor coefficients of (1+x)^p. The radius is inherited from the same geometric limitation that already governed 1/(1-x).
